article_title: Go Blocks Trust in Compromised eMudhra Intermediate CAs Under CVE-2026-111943, and Cilium, Terraform and OpenTofu Ship Releases

content_preview.title: Go Blocks Trust in Compromised eMudhra Intermediate CAs Under CVE-2026-111943, and Cilium, Terraform and OpenTofu Ship Releases
content_preview.summary: Go 1.26.10 filters certificate chains through a set of eMudhra intermediates; Cilium, Terraform and OpenTofu have since released builds, and the Go thread debates the hardcoded approach.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Go 1.26.10, which the Go project [lists as released on 2026-10-19](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release), blocks trust in a small set of intermediate certificates. The [Go issue for CVE-2026-111943](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/82345) says the change is made "due to specific security concerns around their operation" and that `Verify` "will now filter out chains which contain these intermediates." editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, What the Go Project Said, Downstream Releases, debate, What We Don't Know). 671 words, inside the News range of 400-1200. Appropriately hedged on everything the sources do not establish.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 10 snapshots (source-0..9.html.gz, HTTP 200, no archive fallback, manifest suspicious_patterns null for all) were read and then re-checked against live GitHub API / go.dev raw text. source-0 (golang/go#82345): issue body verbatim contains 'We're blocking trust in a small set of intermediate certificates due to specific security concerns around their operation.', 'Verify will now filter out chains which contain these intermediates...', 'We highly recommend immediately upgrading to this release.' and 'This is CVE-2026-111943 and Go issue https://go.dev/issue/82345' - so the CVE id comes from the Go issue itself. Issue title matches. The issue body does not name eMudhra; the name appears in thread comments (zhangyoufu lists Censys entries with eMudhra subject DNs; x0wllaar says they were 'revoked due to `cACompromise` on Oct 18-19 as per [CCADB]') - the article labels both as participant comments and says the Herald did not check certificate records (correct handling). The 'trivial private key' comment (DragonWork) is absent from the article. Quotes verified verbatim: Drugoy ('Such extra filtering isn't a job for a programming language's standard package / lib.'); FiloSottile (three quotes, including 'the keys are compromised and their certificates revoked' and 'short of hardcoding them in code like this'); rolandshoemaker ('We were made aware of the underlying issue here yesterday (Monday)', 'purposefully somewhat vague ... in order to not give attackers a headstart', 'release a safe Go version as quickly as possible'). Speaker names are GitHub usernames; nobody is blamed. source-1 (go.dev/doc/devel/release): 'go1.26.10 (released 2026-10-19) includes security fixes to the crypto/x509 package' - confirmed; page does not mention eMudhra or the CVE, as the article says. source-2/3/4 (Cilium v1.20.4, v1.19.10, v1.18.16): each body states 'Out-of-band security patch release to fix CVE-2026-111943 (golang/go#82345): upgrades Go to 1.26.10 so that the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates are no longer trusted'; GitHub published_at for all three is 2026-10-23 (14:51 UTC) - confirmed. source-5 (Terraform v1.16.7): body dated 'October 22, 2026' with the quoted NOTES line verbatim; source-6 (v1.17.0): dated 'October 21, 2026', same note verbatim. source-7 (terraform PR 39417 'Bump Go version to 1.26.10', merged 2026-10-21): quote 'We usually don't include Go version bumps in the changelog, but I've added a note for all versions as this CVE will probably cause some disruption.' verbatim. source-8/9 (OpenTofu v1.13.2, v1.12.9): both list 'Filter out compromised intermediate certificates' under SECURITY ADVISORIES; GitHub published_at 2026-10-21 for both - confirmed. IMPORTANT: neither OpenTofu release body mentions eMudhra, CVE-2026-111943 or Go 1.26.10 (PRs #4750/#4751, not cited, are titled '...Upgrade go version to include filtering of the compromised intermediate certificates'). The article's OpenTofu bullet quotes the notes accurately, but the Overview sentence says the downstream projects 'shipped releases built on the fixed toolchain', which for OpenTofu is not stated in any cited source - filed as a clarification. Scanner/pattern hits: none (suspicious_patterns null on all sources; chief:review produced no REJECT finding). Allowlist: github.com and go.dev both present in config/source_allowlist.txt. Independent-source note: all sources are first-party project pages; this is a News piece, not an Analysis, so the Analysis independence rule does not apply.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: CVE-2026-111943, the 2026-10-19 Go 1.26.10 date, Cilium Oct 23, Terraform Oct 21/22, OpenTofu Oct 21 and all quotes verified. 'Compromised' framing: the headline term is supported by vendor statements in the sources (Cilium and Terraform release notes say 'compromised eMudhra intermediate CA') and by Go maintainer FiloSottile ('the keys are compromised and their certificates revoked'); the body attributes the eMudhra name to downstream notes and thread participants, and attributes the revocation/cACompromise claim to a commenter as unverified. No claim of wrongdoing by eMudhra is made beyond what the sources say; the article explicitly notes no primary eMudhra statement was found and that how the keys were compromised is not described. One imprecision: the Overview's 'built on the fixed toolchain' for OpenTofu is not supported by the cited OpenTofu notes (see correction).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributed, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Pushback in the thread is presented alongside the maintainers' reply.
editor_notes.originality: New story. The only overlapping coverage is a Node.js security-release article (2026-10/22) that mentions the same eMudhra CA update as one item among ten CVEs; this article covers the Go standard library response and Go-based downstream projects, a distinct angle. Linked as related.
concerns: Overview says downstream projects 'shipped releases built on the fixed toolchain, including ... OpenTofu', but the cited OpenTofu release notes only say 'Filter out compromised intermediate certificates' and do not mention Go 1.26.10, the CVE or eMudhra (clarification filed).

Headline uses 'Compromised eMudhra Intermediate CAs' unattributed; supported by Cilium/Terraform release notes and a Go maintainer, but the Go issue itself does not name eMudhra. Body attribution is adequate; left as-is.
recommendations: When a downstream note does not name the CVE or toolchain version, say so explicitly rather than grouping it with releases that do.
Consider citing OpenTofu PRs #4750/#4751 when asserting the Go upgrade.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed coverage of a security response affecting the Go standard library and widely used infrastructure tooling, with defamation-sensitive claims about eMudhra properly attributed and hedged. One clarification needed on OpenTofu's toolchain claim. Featured candidacy: 2 - a distrusted CA hardcoded into the Go standard library and shipped across Cilium, Terraform and OpenTofu is a notable security incident for a broad developer audience, though the article is a secondary, release-notes-level account.
